set.body:
Scheduling lane: later. Current plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md. Live dependency edges supersede historical sequencing below.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19; governing docs/refactor/PLAN.md.
Outside the current preview path; preserve evidence and acceptance scope, resume only for a named consumer or demonstrated blocking defect.

Original scope retained below for evidence; fleet procedure/assignments are historical and do not govern single-developer work.

TWO CROSS-REPO FINDINGS, surfaced while authorizing a StoryAtlas candidate. Neither is urgent
tonight and both are the kind of thing that is discovered at the worst possible moment.

1. TONIGHT'S WORK IS UNPUSHED. `origin/main` is at 7385cf9. ELEVEN commits sit only in this
   checkout: the ledger-vs-git rule, the gate-inert rule, the backgrounded-gate rule, the
   shared-tree rule, SourceView.measuredPosition and both call sites, ADR 0007, its wording fix,
   the summon-door probes, and board ops. `codex-storymodel-release`, who performs the mechanical
   push, is EXPIRED.

   Nobody noticed because everybody gates locally against the working tree, so the absence of a
   remote is invisible until you need one. I am not pushing: rule 5 assigns that to release, and my
   own rule puts the full court before a push -- which is the court that is waiting on grok's two
   reviews anyway. So the sequence is: reviews -> merge -> ONE full court -> release pushes. It
   just needs to actually happen rather than being assumed.

2. STORYATLAS IS NOT PROTECTED BY ANY OF IT, AND WILL NOT BE FOR SOME TIME. storyatlas4s pins
   storymodel4s at 3cf704a (their build.sbt:32) and fetches it FROM GITHUB. That commit is on our
   main and is **148 COMMITS BEHIND IT**. StoryAtlas therefore builds against a storymodel4s that
   predates sweep 2, predates measuredPosition, predates every construction boundary closed this
   week.

   ANYONE REASONING "storymodel4s sealed that type, so the atlas is safe" IS WRONG BY 148 COMMITS.
   The pin cannot move until finding 1 is resolved, because the commits are not on GitHub to pin to.

AND THE MISTAKE I ALMOST MADE, which is the reusable part. To gate the StoryAtlas candidate I was
about to pass `-Dstoryatlas4s.storymodel4s.build=<local path>` and point it at this working tree.
That would have tested the candidate against TONIGHT'S UNREVIEWED, UNPUSHED storymodel4s instead of
against its DECLARED DEPENDENCY, and produced a green that said nothing about what will actually
ship. An override that makes a build succeed locally by substituting a different dependency is not
a convenience -- IT IS A GATE MEASURING SOMETHING OTHER THAN THE THING SHIPPED, which is the same
family as a red gate that measured infrastructure.

If you gate a sibling build, gate it against its PIN. If the pin is too old to work with, that is a
finding about the pin, not a reason to override it.

Filing the pin bump as its own bead. It is blocked on the push and should not ride along with
anything.
set.title: [later] storyatlas4s pins storymodel4s 50 commits behind main (3a6d73d8 at storyatlas4s/build.sbt:36), so sealing work on main does not protect the atlas
